tituloOriginal: Delayed stomach herniation through ruptured left hemidiaphragm
achadosOriginais: Peristent defect of the left hemidiaphragm with interval herniation of the stomach through the defect. A collar sign is present, where the herniated stomach is compressed by the diaphragm as it traverses the defect. Defect in the left diaphragm with mesenteric fat herniating through the defect.

tituloOriginal: Traumatic small bowel and mesenteric injuries
achadosOriginais: An ill-defined area of mesenteric contusion is seen in the lower abdominal and pelvic midline, manifested by mesenteric fat stranding and small hematomas . Mild free intraperitoneal hyperattenuating fluid is present in the pelvis and right perirenal space and the Morison pouch , in keeping with hemoperitoneum. Adjacent ileal loop demonstrates mild circumferential wall thickening and increased luminal attenuation, suggesting hemorrhage due to contusion and/or ischemia secondary to the adjacent mesenteric injury. Distally, intraluminal small bowel feces sign indicates slow transit. Proximal small bowel loops are predominantly fluid-filled consistent with ileus or an evolving obstruction. The stomach is distended with a large intraluminal air fluid level. No solid organ injuries.
The cardiac silhouette is enlarged from chest wall to chest wall. Normal aerated lung is absent from the left lower zone and CPA indicating pleural effusion.

Massive cardiomegaly (CTR of 0.75). Cephalisation of left upper lobe pulmonary veins. Abnormal aortic contour with figure of 3 sign . Bilateral inferior rib notching with sparing of the first 2 ribs bilaterally. No pleural effusion or hilar enlargement. No pruning of pulmonary vessels.

Enlarged heart shadow with down tilting of cardiac apex , double density sign of right heart , enlargement of left atrial appendage (third mogul sign), and splaying of carina. No evidence of pleural effusion.

tituloOriginal: Aortic valve calcifications visible on plain radiograph
achadosOriginais: "Life vest" device in place. Trace pleural effusions, no edema or pneumonia. Aortic valve calcifications . Interval transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
Pericardial calcifications , mild enlargement cardiac silhouette, no edema, pneumonia or pleural effusion.
Lungs and pleural spaces are clear. No focal consolidation or collapse. The cardiac silhouette is enlarged even allowing for AP projection with a focal bulge at the apex .

The mobile, erect chest X-ray demonstrates multichamber cardiomegaly. A left subclavian access dual-chamber external pacemaker is present, with the right atrial and right ventricular apex leads satisfactorily sited and non-fragmented. There is a median sternotomy with multiple cerclage wires . However, there is the noted absence of mediastinal surgical clips. There are three radiopaque rings at the anatomical level of the aortic valve, better visualized in the window-adjusted zoomed and reverse windows . The lung fields are hyperinflated but clear. Image courtesy: Dr MN Patel.

tituloOriginal: Thoracic aortic aneurysm - hilum overlay sign
achadosOriginais: Minimal opacity at the left lower lobe. Mediastinal widening with left-sided mediastinal opacity , with a thin, dense wall that continues with the aortic arch. The left hilum is seen through the lucent lesion. Further assessment with contrast-enhanced CT is advised. Thoracic spondylotic changes. Diffuse osteopenia. Right glenohumeral osteoarthritis.
There is massive enlargement of the main and left , and right pulmonary arteries, compatible with the history of pulmonary hypertension. The lungs are clear.

tituloOriginal: Scimitar syndrome with right lung hypoplasia
achadosOriginais: Reduced bilateral lung volumes (right > left). Tracheal deviation and mediastinal shift to the right. Right mid to lower zone opacities.
Dextrocardia . Gastric bubble in the right upper abdomen. Right lower lung bronchiectasis and linear opacities with silhouetting of the right hemidiaphragm.

Curvilinear lucency outlines the left cardiac border suggestive of pneumopericardium . In addition, there are some linear lucencies extending to the cervical region compatible with subcutaneous emphysema . No confluent consolidation or atelectasis. Heart size and cardiomediastinal contour are normal.
